keywords: how to get clients in singapore
intro: Four outbound campaigns in Singapore: three Singapore firms in finance, insurance and staffing, and an Indian pharma developer opening licensing talks. Every number below comes from a real campaign.

audiences.title: Singapore-based firms
audiences.body: Outsourced finance, insurance broking and staffing firms that rely on referrals and want earlier conversations with business owners, finance heads and HR leaders.

audiences.title: Companies reaching Singapore and its regional teams
audiences.body: Indian companies looking for licensing, distribution or commercial partners among Singapore-based businesses and the regional teams based there.

plays.title: Open on a specific finance need
plays.body: A Singapore CFO and accounting firm contacted founders and finance leaders about specific needs, such as monthly management reports or senior finance support, instead of a service list.

plays.title: Share a non-confidential summary first
plays.body: An Indian specialty pharma developer reached business development and licensing leaders with an approved, non-confidential product summary. Confidentiality agreements came only once talks progressed.

plays.title: Ask about upcoming needs, not open roles
plays.body: A Singapore staffing firm with uneven demand asked HR, finance and operations leaders about upcoming temporary staffing needs, then qualified by role, duration and start date.

rulesBody: Singapore's Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) governs how personal data is collected and used, and the Spam Control Act covers unsolicited commercial email sent in bulk. We keep volumes low, contact business decision-makers only and honour every opt-out. Check specifics with counsel.
timingBody: Singapore is 2.5 hours ahead of India. Messages go out on Singapore weekday mornings, which is early morning in India, and meetings fit easily into an Indian working day.
